content.value_statement: Quetrex teams need consistent feature work across TypeScript, Next.js, validation, UI, and testing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to review and implement features against those standards.
actual_capabilities: Checks TypeScript strict mode expectations, including explicit types, unknown usage, and avoiding any.
Distinguishes Next.js Server Components from Client Components and flags async client components.
Requires Zod validation for API route input before using request data.
Promotes ShadCN UI components, React Hook Form, and Zod for forms.
Guides a TDD workflow with failing tests, implementation, passing tests, and refactoring.
Reports violations with file, line, explanation, and a corrected pattern.
limitations: Focused on Quetrex conventions, so recommendations may not fit unrelated projects.
Uses read and search tools only; it does not run tests or modify files by itself.
Relies on project context files when available; missing docs reduce accuracy.
References November 2025 standards; teams should verify current dependency behavior.

use_cases.title: Feature Implementation
use_cases.description: Implement new Quetrex features while following TDD, strict typing, App Router patterns, Zod validation, and ShadCN UI conventions.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review pull requests for architecture drift, validation gaps, UI inconsistency, and missing tests before merge.

use_cases.title: Legacy Refactoring
use_cases.description: Refactor older Quetrex code while preserving documented project patterns and coverage expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Quetrex feature plan for architecture issues. Check TypeScript strict mode, App Router usage, Zod validation, ShadCN UI, and TDD steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request with the Quetrex architecture rules. List each violation with file, line, reason, and a corrected approach.

prompt_templates.title: Guide Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help implement this Quetrex feature using TDD. Start with failing tests, then guide strict TypeScript, validation, and approved UI patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this refactor for Quetrex compliance. Compare current code against project patterns, security rules, coverage targets, and App Router boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review a new project creation API route for Quetrex standards.
output: Identifies missing request validation before business logic.
Explains why Zod validation is required for API input.
Recommends a corrected pattern using a validated request body.

output_examples.input: Check a dashboard component that mixes server data loading and client state.
output: Separates server data loading from client-only interaction.
Flags an async client component as a framework violation.
Suggests a server wrapper with a focused interactive child component.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a Quetrex feature is ready for review.
output: Checks that tests were written before implementation.
Compares affected files with coverage expectations.
Lists remaining architecture and security issues before merge.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, affected files, and relevant Quetrex docs before asking for review.
Ask for violations with file and line numbers when reviewing existing code.
Use the guidance before implementation and again before opening a pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a generic Next.js reviewer without Quetrex context.
Do not ask it to skip tests, validation, or security rules for speed.
Do not treat code examples as automatic fixes without adapting them to your project.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for Quetrex projects using TypeScript, Next.js App Router, ShadCN UI, Zod, and TDD.

faq.question: Can it write code for me?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation and provide examples, but its declared tools are limited to reading and searching.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It describes a TDD process and coverage targets, but it does not execute test commands.

faq.question: Can it review pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify architecture violations and explain each issue with a recommended fix.

faq.question: Does it handle security review?
faq.answer: It checks documented patterns such as hardcoded secrets, input validation, and SQL injection risks.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Quetrex?
faq.answer: Partly. The guidance may help similar stacks, but Quetrex-specific rules remain its primary focus.
